readings.section: The Rise of the Right Arm
readings.title: The Anointing of David
readings.subtitle: Samuel is Sent to Bethlehem
readings.text: [1 Samuel 16:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“How long are you going to mourn for Sha’ul, seeing <dn>I</dn> have rejected him from reigning over Yisra’ěl? Fill your horn with oil, and go, <dn>I</dn> am sending you to Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite. For <dn>I</dn> have seen among his sons a sovereign for <dn>Myself</dn>.”</dq> [2] And Shemu’ěl said, “How would I go? When Sha’ul hears it, he shall kill me.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Take a heifer with you, and say, ‘<dn>I</dn> have come to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq> [3] <dq>“And you shall invite Yishai to the slaughtering, then let <dn>Me</dn> show you <dn>את</dn> what to do. And you shall anoint for <dn>Me</dn> <dn>את</dn> the one <dn>I</dn> say to you.”</dq> [4] And Shemu’ěl did <dn>את</dn> what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, and went to Běyth Leḥem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, “Do you come in peace?” [5] And he said, “In peace. I have come to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Set yourselves apart, and you shall come with <dn>את</dn> me to the slaughtering.” And he set <dn>את</dn> Yishai and <dn>את</dn> his sons apart, and invited them to the slaughtering. [6] And it came to be, when they came, that he saw <dn>את</dn> Eliyaḇ and thought, “The anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is indeed before <dn>Him</dn>.” [7] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because <dn>I</dn> have refused him, for not as man sees, for man looks at the eyes, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looks at the heart.”</dq> [8] Then Yishai called Aḇinaḏaḇ, and made him pass before Shemu’ěl. And he said, “Neither has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chosen this one.” [9] Next Yishai made Shammah pass by. And he said, “Neither has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chosen this one.” [10] And Yishai made seven of his sons pass before Shemu’ěl. And Shemu’ěl said to Yishai, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not chosen these.” [11] And Shemu’ěl said to Yishai, “Are these all the young men?” And he said, “There remains yet the youngest, and see, he is tending the sheep.” And Shemu’ěl said to Yishai, “Send and bring him, for we do not turn round till he comes here.” [12] And he sent and brought him in. And he was ruddy, with bright eyes, and handsome. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Arise, anoint him, for this is the one!”</dq> [13] And Shemu’ěl took <dn>את</dn> the horn of oil and anointed <dn>את</dn> him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Daviḏ from that day and onwards. And Shemu’ěl arose and went to Ramah.

readings.section: The Rise of the Right Arm
readings.title: David in Saul's Court
readings.subtitle: The Lyre Player Soothes the King
readings.text: [14] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned aside from Sha’ul, and an evil spirit from <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> troubled him. [15] And the servants of Sha’ul said to him, “Look, now, an evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> is troubling you. [16] “Please, let our master command your servants who are before you, to seek out a man who is a skilled player on the lyre. And it shall be that when the evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> is upon you, that he shall play with his hand, and you be well.” [17] And Sha’ul said to his servants, “Please get me a man that plays well, and bring him to me.” [18] And one of the servants answered and said, “Look, I have seen a son of Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite, who knows how to play, a brave one, and a man of battle, and skilled in words, and a handsome man. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with him.” [19] So Sha’ul sent messengers to Yishai, and said, “Send me <dn>את</dn> your son Daviḏ, who is with the sheep.” [20] And Yishai took a donkey loaded with bread, and a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by his son Daviḏ to Sha’ul. [21] And Daviḏ came to Sha’ul and stood before him. And he loved him greatly, and he became his armour-bearer. [22] Sha’ul therefore sent to Yishai, saying, “Please let Daviḏ stand before me, for he has found favour in my eyes.” [23] And it came to be, whenever the evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> was upon Sha’ul, that Daviḏ would take <dn>את</dn> a lyre and play it with his hand. Then Sha’ul would become refreshed and well, and the evil spirit would leave him.

readings.section: The Rise of the Right Arm
readings.title: The Philistine Champion
readings.subtitle: Goliath Defies the Armies of Israel
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:1] And the Philistines had gathered <dn>את</dn> their armies for battle, and came together at Soḵoh, which belongs to Yehuḏah, and encamped between Soḵoh and Azěqah, in Ephes Dammim. [2] And Sha’ul and the men of Yisra’ěl were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Ělah, and drew up in battle array to meet the Philistines. [3] And the Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, and Yisra’ěl stood on a mountain on the other side, with the valley between them. [4] Then a champion came out from the camp of the Philistines, named Golyath, from Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span. [5] And a bronze helmet was on his head, and he was armed with a scaled armour, and the weight of the coat was five thousand sheqels of bronze, [6] and bronze shin guards on his legs and a bronze spear between his shoulders. [7] And the wood of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and his iron spearhead weighed six hundred sheqels, and a shield-bearer went before him. [8] And he stood and shouted to the armies of Yisra’ěl, and said to them, “Why have you come out to line up for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and you the servants of Sha’ul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me. [9] “If he is able to fight with <dn>את</dn> me, and shall strike me, then we shall be your servants. But if I overcome him and shall strike him, then you shall be our servants and serve <dn>את</dn> us.” [10] Then the Philistine said, “This day I shall reproach <dn>את</dn> the armies of Yisra’ěl. Give me a man, and let us fight together.” [11] And Sha’ul and all Yisra’ěl heard <dn>את</dn> these words of the Philistine, and they were broken down and in great fear.

readings.section: The Rise of the Right Arm
readings.title: David Arrives at the Camp
readings.subtitle: The Shepherd Hears the Reproach
readings.text: [12] Now Daviḏ was the son of that Ephrathite of Běyth Leḥem in Yehuḏah, whose name was Yishai, and he had eight sons, and in the days of Sha’ul the man was old among men. [13] And the three oldest sons of Yishai went, they had gone to follow Sha’ul to the battle, and the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliyaḇ the first-born, and his second Aḇinaḏaḇ, and the third Shammah. [14] And Daviḏ was the youngest. And the three oldest followed Sha’ul, [15] but Daviḏ went and returned from Sha’ul to feed <dn>את</dn> his father’s sheep at Běyth Leḥem. [16] And for forty days the Philistine drew near, morning and evening, and took his stand. [17] Then Yishai said to his son Daviḏ, “Please take to your brothers an ěphah of this dried grain and these ten loaves, and run to your brothers at the camp. [18] “And take <dn>את</dn> these ten cheeses to the commander of the thousand, and see how <dn>את</dn> your brothers are, and bring back <dn>את</dn> news of them.” [19] For Sha’ul and they and all the men of Yisra’ěl were in the Valley of Ělah, fighting with the Philistines. [20] And Daviḏ rose up early in the morning, and left <dn>את</dn> the sheep with a herdsman, and took and went as Yishai had commanded him. And he came to the camp as the army was going out to the fight, and they shouted for the battle. [21] And Yisra’ěl and the Philistines drew up in battle array, army against army. [22] And Daviḏ left <dn>את</dn> his supplies in the hand of the keeper of the supplies, and ran to the army, and came and greeted his brothers. [23] And he was speaking with them and saw the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Golyath by name, coming up from the armies of the Philistines. And he spoke according to the same words, and Daviḏ heard. [24] And all the men of Yisra’ěl, when they saw <dn>את</dn> the man, ran from him and were in great fear. [25] And the men of Yisra’ěl said, “Have you seen this man who has come up? For he has come up to reproach <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl. And it shall be that the man who strikes him, the sovereign is going to enrich him with great riches, and give him <dn>את</dn> his daughter, and give <dn>את</dn> his father’s house exemption in Yisra’ěl.” [26] And Daviḏ spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done for the man who strikes <dn>את</dn> this Philistine and shall take away reproach from Yisra’ěl? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should reproach the armies of the living <dn>Elohim</dn>?” [27] And the people answered him according to this word, saying, “This is what is done for the man who strikes him.” [28] And Eliyaḇ his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men. And Eliyaḇ’s displeasure burned against Daviḏ, and he said, “Why did you come down here? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know <dn>את</dn> your pride and <dn>את</dn> the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle.” [29] And Daviḏ said, “Now what have I done? Was it not but a word?” [30] And he turned around from him toward another and said the same word. And these people answered him a word like the first word. [31] And when the words which Daviḏ spoke were heard, they reported them to Sha’ul, and he sent for him.

readings.section: The Rise of the Right Arm
readings.title: The Fall of Goliath
readings.subtitle: The Battle Belongs to YeHoVaH
readings.text: [32] And Daviḏ said to Sha’ul, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him, your servant is going, and shall fight with this Philistine.” [33] And Sha’ul said to Daviḏ, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are but a youth, and he a man of battle from his youth.” [34] Then Daviḏ said to Sha’ul, “Your servant has been tending sheep for his father, and when a lion or <dn>את</dn> a bear came and took a lamb out of the flock, [35] I went out after it and struck it, and rescued it from its mouth. And when it rose against me, I took hold of it by its beard, and struck it and killed it. [36] “Your servant has stricken both <dn>את</dn> lion and bear. And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, seeing he has reproached the armies of the living <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [37] And Daviḏ said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, <dn>He</dn> does deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.” And Sha’ul said to Daviḏ, “Go, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you!” [38] And Sha’ul dressed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ with his garments, and he put a bronze helmet on his head, and put a coat of armour on him. [39] And Daviḏ girded <dn>את</dn> his sword over his garments, and began to go, but he had not tried them. Then Daviḏ said to Sha’ul, “I am not able to go with these, for I have not tried them.” So Daviḏ took them off. [40] And he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put <dn>את</dn> them in a shepherd’s bag, in a pouch which he had, and his sling was in his hand. And he drew near to the Philistine. [41] And the Philistine came, and began drawing near to Daviḏ, and the man who bore the shield went before him. [42] And when the Philistine looked about and saw <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ, he despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy and of handsome appearance. [43] And the Philistine said to Daviḏ, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ by his mighty ones. [44] And the Philistine said to Daviḏ, “Come to me, and I give <dn>את</dn> your flesh to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field!” [45] But Daviḏ said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin. But I come to you in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the armies of Yisra’ěl, whom you have reproached. [46] “This day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall deliver you into my hand, and I shall strike you and take <dn>את</dn> your head from you, and give the carcasses of the camp of the Philistines today to the birds of the heavens and the wild beasts of the earth, so that all the earth know that <dn>Elohim</dn> is for Yisra’ěl, [47] and all this assembly know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not save with sword and spear, for the battle belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> you into our hands.” [48] And it came to be, when the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet Daviḏ, that Daviḏ hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine. [49] And Daviḏ put <dn>את</dn> his hand in his bag and took out a stone, and slung it and struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistine on his forehead, so that the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground. [50] Thus Daviḏ was stronger than the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistine and killed him, and there was no sword in the hand of Daviḏ. [51] Then Daviḏ ran and stood over the Philistine, and took <dn>את</dn> his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off <dn>את</dn> his head with it. And when the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled. [52] And the men of Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah arose and shouted, and pursued <dn>את</dn> the Philistines as far as the entrance of the valley and to the gates of Eqron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell along the way to Sha‛arayim, even as far as Gath and Eqron. [53] Then the children of Yisra’ěl turned back from chasing the Philistines, and they plundered <dn>את</dn> their camps. [54] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> the head of the Philistine and brought it to Yerushalayim, but he put <dn>את</dn> his weapons in his tent. [55] And when Sha’ul saw <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ going out against the Philistine, he said to Aḇněr, the commander of the army, “Aḇněr, whose son is this youth?” And Aḇněr said, “As your being lives, O sovereign, I do not know.” [56] And the sovereign said, “Ask whose son this young man is.” [57] And when Daviḏ returned from the striking of the Philistine, Aḇněr took him and brought him before Sha’ul with the head of the Philistine in his hand. [58] And Sha’ul said to him, “Whose son are you, young man?” And Daviḏ said, “The son of your servant Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite.”
